description: The single source for every CHECK-constrained vocabulary the server enforces and the projection renders. mcp-server/src/vocabulary.ts and materializer/amanuensis_materializer/vocabulary.py are generated from this file by mcp-server/scripts/gen-vocabulary.mjs; the SQL CHECK literals in src/schema.sql are not generated but are asserted against it by --check-sql.

values.label: Open
values.meaning: No terminal resolution event has been recorded; the item is still open.
values.cannot_justify: that the defect is still reproducible at the repository head

values.label: Accepted
values.meaning: The behavior is recorded as understood and acceptable; it is not an open defect.
values.cannot_justify: that the judgement was revisited at the repository head

values.label: Ruled out
values.meaning: The candidate problem was overturned by evidence or adversarial review.
values.cannot_justify: that no related defect exists at the same locus

values.label: Unverified fix
values.meaning: A repair is recorded, but independent fix evidence has not yet closed the finding.
values.cannot_justify: that the defect is gone at the repository head

values.label: Verified fixed
values.meaning: A later revision contains a repair backed by recorded verification evidence.
values.cannot_justify: that the repair is still present at the repository head

finding_status.note: The coarse mutable projection of the resolution events; finding_resolution_state is the authority.

values.label: Confirmed defect
values.meaning: A defect supported by evidence and retained after adversarial review.
values.cannot_justify: that the defect is unrepaired at the repository head; the resolution events are the authority

values.label: Accepted behavior
values.meaning: The observed behavior is real and judged to be intended or acceptable.
values.cannot_justify: that the judgement was revisited at the repository head

values.label: Fixed
values.meaning: The defect was confirmed at an earlier revision and is recorded as addressed later.
values.cannot_justify: that verification evidence closed the finding; only a verified-fixed event carries that

values.label: Ruled out
values.meaning: The candidate problem was overturned by evidence or adversarial review.
values.cannot_justify: that no related defect exists at the same locus

standing_state.note: Computed by the file_standing view and the unledgered probe; no column stores it.

values.label: No record
values.meaning: No file_ledger row names this path in any subsystem.
values.cannot_justify: "there are no findings here"; "this file is out of scope"

values.label: Excluded
values.meaning: A ledger row classifies the path as generated, vendored, irrelevant, or deferred with a recorded reason.
values.cannot_justify: any claim about the file's content or behavior
values.authorizes: the recorded exclusion reason and classification

values.label: In scope, not yet read
values.meaning: A ledger row classifies the path candidate: it participates in a subsystem, and no one has read it.
values.cannot_justify: any claim about content, behavior, or the absence of defects
values.authorizes: that this file participates in its owning subsystem

values.label: Examined
values.meaning: A ledger row classifies the path examined, it is not stale, and its examination revision resolves in the workspace.
values.cannot_justify: claims about symbols no evidence cites; the absence of defects
values.authorizes: current claims whose evidence cites this file

values.label: Examined, since changed
values.meaning: The path was examined, and drift, absence, or an unreachable examination revision has withdrawn that reading's currency.
values.cannot_justify: any current claim at the repository head
values.authorizes: a dated historical reading, attributed to its examination revision

values.label: No longer in the repository
values.meaning: A scope_gaps row of kind absent, or a ledger row whose stale_reason is absent.
values.cannot_justify: anything at the repository head
values.authorizes: that the path was once surveyed

values.label: Owners disagree
values.meaning: Two or more owning subsystems record different standing states for the same path.
values.cannot_justify: anything the weakest owner state cannot justify
values.authorizes: only what the weakest owner state authorizes

stale_reason.note: file_ledger.stale_reason carries no CHECK constraint; the writers are detect_changes and the standing reachability probe.

values.label: Changed since examination
values.meaning: The file's content differs from the revision it was examined at.
values.cannot_justify: that the recorded reading is wrong, only that it is no longer current

values.label: Gone from the repository
values.meaning: The examined path is no longer tracked in the workspace.
values.cannot_justify: anything about the current tree at that path

values.label: Examination revision cannot be compared
values.meaning: The examination revision could not be diffed against the current head, so drift could not be computed.
values.cannot_justify: that the file did or did not change

values.label: Examination revision is not an ancestor
values.meaning: The examination revision resolves in the workspace but is not an ancestor of the current head.
values.cannot_justify: any current claim at the repository head

values.label: In scope, not yet read
values.meaning: The path participates in a subsystem and has not been read.
values.cannot_justify: any claim about content or behavior

values.label: Examined
values.meaning: The path was read and its reading is anchored to an examination revision.
values.cannot_justify: claims about symbols no evidence cites

values.label: Generated
values.meaning: The path is build or projection output and is not read as a source of claims.
values.cannot_justify: anything about the generator that produced it

values.label: Vendored
values.meaning: The path is third-party code carried in the tree and is not surveyed.
values.cannot_justify: anything about the upstream project's behavior

values.label: Ruled irrelevant
values.meaning: The path was judged to carry nothing the survey needs.
values.cannot_justify: that the judgement was re-examined at the repository head

values.label: Deferred
values.meaning: The path is in scope but deliberately left unread, with the reason recorded.
values.cannot_justify: any claim about content or behavior

values.label: Unmapped
values.meaning: This subsystem has not yet been surveyed; no architectural claims are authorized.
values.cannot_justify: any claim about this subsystem's behavior

values.label: Scoping
values.meaning: Only the subsystem boundary and file scope are established so far.
values.authorizes: which files are in scope for this subsystem
values.cannot_justify: any behavioral claim; file scope is all that is established

values.label: Structural
values.meaning: Types, state, flows, and concurrency are mapped; correctness claims are not yet authorized.
values.authorizes: claims about types, state containers, flows, and the concurrency model
values.cannot_justify: any correctness claim

values.label: Concerns
values.meaning: Structural mapping is complete and concern-by-concern review is in progress.
values.authorizes: concern review decisions that cite evidence
values.cannot_justify: that a finding survived adversarial challenge

values.label: Adversarial
values.meaning: Candidate conclusions are being challenged; treat them as provisional.
values.authorizes: provisional conclusions while the challenge pass runs; a finding counts as survived only where its recorded adversarial evidence or terminal review aggregation says so
values.cannot_justify: that the challenge pass has finished

values.label: Mapped
values.meaning: Survey complete through structural analysis, concern review, and adversarial challenge.
values.authorizes: the recorded survey through structural analysis, concern review, and adversarial challenge
values.cannot_justify: that the reading is current at the repository head

values.label: Deferred
values.meaning: This subsystem is intentionally outside the active survey plan.
values.cannot_justify: anything about this subsystem's behavior

vocabulary_discharge.note: The three states a subsystem's domain vocabulary can be in at the advance to 'structural'. Discharge or decline, never a floor: one anchored term is enough, 'none' is a real and common answer that has to be said out loud, and a subsystem nobody asked is a third state that is never collapsed into the second.

values.label: Terms recorded
values.meaning: The subsystem carries at least one vocabulary term scoped to it whose first_seen anchor still resolves: the token parses, its revision is reachable, and its path exists in that revision's tree.
values.cannot_justify: that the recorded terms are the ones a reader most needs, or that the list is complete; one anchored term discharges the obligation and no count is required

values.label: Declared none
values.meaning: A reader examined the subsystem and declared, at a recorded revision and in an attributed session, that it carries no domain vocabulary of its own.
values.cannot_justify: that the judgement is true; the substrate can require that it be made, attributed and dated, and cannot check whether the subsystem really coins nothing

values.label: Not recorded
values.meaning: Neither a term nor a declination has been recorded for this subsystem, so nobody has answered the question either way.
values.cannot_justify: that the subsystem has no domain vocabulary; nothing was asked and nothing was answered, which is not the same as 'none'

evidence_kind.note: Ordered strongest first; SKILL.md publishes the same order as the kind ladder.

values.label: Code verified
values.meaning: The implementation was read and the stated behavior was verified directly.
values.cannot_justify: behavior at any revision other than the one cited

values.label: Runtime observed
values.meaning: The behavior was observed in a running system and the observation was recorded.
values.cannot_justify: that the same behavior holds under other inputs or configurations

values.label: Contract stated
values.meaning: An explicit schema, type, or behavioral contract states this claim.
values.cannot_justify: that the implementation honors the contract

values.label: Test observed
values.meaning: A test run or recorded observation demonstrates this behavior.
values.cannot_justify: behavior outside what the test exercises

values.label: Config asserted
values.meaning: Configuration states the behavior, but runtime behavior was not independently verified.
values.cannot_justify: that this configuration is the one in effect

values.label: Docs asserted
values.meaning: Project documentation states the claim; implementation agreement is not yet verified.
values.cannot_justify: that the implementation matches the documentation

values.label: Comment asserted
values.meaning: A code comment states the claim; the implementation was not verified against it.
values.cannot_justify: that the comment is current with the code beside it

values.label: Name inferred
values.meaning: The claim is inferred from a symbol name and should be treated as weak evidence.
values.cannot_justify: any correctness claim; a name is not an implementation

values.label: Pattern matched
values.meaning: The claim matches a known pattern and is only a scoping signal.
values.cannot_justify: any claim about what this locus actually does

evidence_quality.note: A disposition's evidence_quality names the strongest evidence row attached to it, so it must be exactly what add_evidence accepts (finding B03-3).

values.label: Code verified
values.meaning: The implementation was read and the stated behavior was verified directly.
values.cannot_justify: behavior at any revision other than the one cited

values.label: Runtime observed
values.meaning: The behavior was observed in a running system and the observation was recorded.
values.cannot_justify: that the same behavior holds under other inputs or configurations

values.label: Contract stated
values.meaning: An explicit schema, type, or behavioral contract states this claim.
values.cannot_justify: that the implementation honors the contract

values.label: Test observed
values.meaning: A test run or recorded observation demonstrates this behavior.
values.cannot_justify: behavior outside what the test exercises

values.label: Config asserted
values.meaning: Configuration states the behavior, but runtime behavior was not independently verified.
values.cannot_justify: that this configuration is the one in effect

values.label: Docs asserted
values.meaning: Project documentation states the claim; implementation agreement is not yet verified.
values.cannot_justify: that the implementation matches the documentation

values.label: Comment asserted
values.meaning: A code comment states the claim; the implementation was not verified against it.
values.cannot_justify: that the comment is current with the code beside it

values.label: Name inferred
values.meaning: The claim is inferred from a symbol name and should be treated as weak evidence.
values.cannot_justify: any correctness claim; a name is not an implementation

values.label: Pattern matched
values.meaning: The claim matches a known pattern and is only a scoping signal.
values.cannot_justify: any claim about what this locus actually does

values.label: Confirmed defect
values.meaning: A defect supported by evidence and retained after adversarial review.
values.cannot_justify: that the defect is unrepaired at the repository head

values.label: Accepted behavior
values.meaning: The observed behavior is real and judged to be intended or acceptable.
values.cannot_justify: that the judgement was revisited at the repository head

values.label: Ruled out
values.meaning: The candidate problem was overturned by evidence or adversarial review.
values.cannot_justify: that no related defect exists at the same locus

values.label: Out of scope
values.meaning: The concern does not apply within this subsystem's declared boundary.
values.cannot_justify: that the concern does not apply elsewhere in the project

values.label: Competing explanations
values.meaning: Multiple explanations remain viable; the evidence does not discriminate.
values.cannot_justify: that any one of the competing explanations is the right one

values.label: Critical
values.meaning: Potential data loss, security failure, privilege escalation, or production outage path.
values.cannot_justify: how likely the path is to be reached; severity is impact, not confidence

values.label: High
values.meaning: Incorrect behavior on a common path, corrupt state, or a seriously wedged workflow.
values.cannot_justify: how confident the finding is; severity is impact, not confidence

values.label: Medium
values.meaning: Incorrect edge-case behavior or a correctness issue with a known workaround.
values.cannot_justify: that the edge case is rare in practice

values.label: Low
values.meaning: Maintainability, clarity, or defensive-coding risk most likely to affect a future change.
values.cannot_justify: that the risk will never be reached

values.label: Pattern
values.meaning: A recurrence noticed in more than one place.
values.cannot_justify: that the recurrence is intentional

values.label: Anomaly
values.meaning: A deviation from the surrounding conventions or expectations.
values.cannot_justify: that the deviation is a defect

values.label: Connection
values.meaning: A relationship noticed across subsystem boundaries.
values.cannot_justify: that the relationship is load-bearing

values.label: Tension
values.meaning: Local correctness that sits awkwardly against global coherence.
values.cannot_justify: that either side is wrong

values.label: Candidate concern
values.meaning: A pattern that might warrant a concern code of its own.
values.cannot_justify: that the concern has been reviewed anywhere

values.label: Domain knowledge
values.meaning: A business rule or domain fact the record cannot supply.
values.cannot_justify: the assumption recorded in its place

values.label: Scope judgment
values.meaning: A scope fence that needs a human to confirm.
values.cannot_justify: that the assumed boundary is the right one

values.label: Priority ranking
values.meaning: A survey order the agent guessed and a reviewer can override.
values.cannot_justify: that the ranking reflects project priorities

values.label: Contradiction
values.meaning: Two credible sources disagree and the record does not settle it.
values.cannot_justify: either reading

values.label: Tooling limit
values.meaning: An operation the agent could not perform.
values.cannot_justify: anything about what that operation would have shown

values.label: Ambiguous evidence
values.meaning: The evidence permits more than one interpretation.
values.cannot_justify: any single interpretation

values.label: Other
values.meaning: A question that fits none of the recorded categories.
values.cannot_justify: anything beyond the question as asked

values.label: Open
values.meaning: No answer has been recorded.
values.cannot_justify: that the question is still the right one to ask

values.label: Answered
values.meaning: A human recorded an answer.
values.cannot_justify: that the answer was applied to the record

values.label: Dismissed
values.meaning: The question was withdrawn without an answer.
values.cannot_justify: that the underlying uncertainty was resolved

values.label: Superseded
values.meaning: A later question or decision replaced this one.
values.cannot_justify: what the replacement decided

field_note_follow_up.note: field_notes.follow_up carries no CHECK: a finding id may also be recorded here, which is how a lead is promoted.

values.label: Open
values.meaning: The lead has not been taken up.
values.cannot_justify: that the lead is still worth taking up

values.label: Dismissed
values.meaning: The lead was closed without becoming a finding.
values.cannot_justify: that the observation behind it was wrong

xref_relationship.note: xrefs.relationship carries no CHECK; these are the canonical values add_xref publishes.

values.label: Shared pattern
values.meaning: Both subsystems implement the same pattern.
values.cannot_justify: that either copy is derived from the other

values.label: Data flow
values.meaning: Data produced by one subsystem is consumed by the other.
values.cannot_justify: the direction of control, only of data

values.label: Dependency
values.meaning: One subsystem depends on the other to do its work.
values.cannot_justify: that the dependency is the only one between them

values.label: Mirrors
values.meaning: The two subsystems maintain parallel structures that must stay in step.
values.cannot_justify: that anything enforces the parallel

values.label: Contention
values.meaning: Both subsystems compete for the same resource.
values.cannot_justify: that the contention is unmanaged

values.label: Temporal coupling
values.meaning: The two must run, or change, in a particular order.
values.cannot_justify: that the order is enforced anywhere

values.label: Observed
values.meaning: The link was seen once in the code and recorded.
values.cannot_justify: that the link is intentional or stable

values.label: Confirmed
values.meaning: The link was checked from both sides.
values.cannot_justify: that the link is architecturally required

values.label: Structural
values.meaning: The link follows from a structure both sides depend on.
values.cannot_justify: that either side is aware of the other

values.label: A supersedes B
values.meaning: The first finding stands and the second is withdrawn.
values.cannot_justify: that the withdrawn finding was wrong about everything it said

values.label: B supersedes A
values.meaning: The second finding stands and the first is withdrawn.
values.cannot_justify: that the withdrawn finding was wrong about everything it said

values.label: Scope distinction
values.meaning: Both findings stand; they apply to scopes the record now distinguishes.
values.cannot_justify: that either finding was re-verified

values.label: Unresolved
values.meaning: The conflict is recorded and not yet settled.
values.cannot_justify: either finding

values.label: Open
values.meaning: The competing explanations have not been analyzed to a verdict.
values.cannot_justify: any one of the competing explanations

values.label: Resolved
values.meaning: This item has a recorded resolution.
values.cannot_justify: that the resolution was independently checked

values.label: Competing explanations
values.meaning: Multiple explanations remain viable; the evidence does not discriminate.
values.cannot_justify: that any one of the competing explanations is the right one

values.label: Observation
values.meaning: Something read directly in the code or an artifact.
values.cannot_justify: why it is that way

values.label: Inference
values.meaning: A conclusion drawn from observations, not read directly.
values.cannot_justify: itself as an observation

values.label: Hypothesis
values.meaning: A candidate explanation offered for testing.
values.cannot_justify: any conclusion until it has been tested

values.label: Open question
values.meaning: A question the record raises and does not answer.
values.cannot_justify: any answer to it

values.label: Direct intent
values.meaning: Intent a human stated.
values.cannot_justify: intent the human did not state

values.label: Inferred intent
values.meaning: Intent attributed from the code or the record, not stated.
values.cannot_justify: that the attributed intent is the actual one

values.label: Decision
values.meaning: A choice recorded with the authority that made it.
values.cannot_justify: that the decision was carried out

claim_subject_type.note: claims.subject_type carries a length CHECK only; the closed vocabulary is enforced by the tool.

values.label: Symbol
values.meaning: A named function, type, or value at a path.
values.cannot_justify: anything about its callers

values.label: Subsystem
values.meaning: A registered subsystem id.
values.cannot_justify: anything about a specific file within it

values.label: Seam
values.meaning: A registered boundary between two subsystems.
values.cannot_justify: either party's internals

values.label: Active
values.meaning: The concern is on the checklist and must be dispositioned.
values.cannot_justify: that any subsystem has dispositioned it

values.label: Retired
values.meaning: The concern was withdrawn from the checklist.
values.cannot_justify: that past dispositions were revisited

values.label: Merged
values.meaning: The concern was folded into another concern code.
values.cannot_justify: anything the target concern has not recorded

values.label: Candidate
values.meaning: The concern was proposed and not yet accepted onto the checklist.
values.cannot_justify: that it is reviewed anywhere

values.label: Onboarding
values.meaning: The first pass, which establishes scope and the survey plan.
values.cannot_justify: any correctness claim

values.label: Survey
values.meaning: The structural and concern-review pass over a subsystem.
values.cannot_justify: that a conclusion survived challenge

values.label: Adversarial
values.meaning: The pass that tries to overturn what the survey concluded.
values.cannot_justify: that nothing was missed

values.label: Refresh
values.meaning: A later pass that re-examines the record against a newer revision.
values.cannot_justify: anything the refresh did not re-read

values.label: Codebase
values.meaning: The recorded account of what the project is, how it works, and which of its territory has not been read.
values.cannot_justify: that unread territory holds no defects

values.label: Unresolved
values.meaning: Records that have not reached a terminal, evidence-backed state at the checked revision.
values.cannot_justify: that a record here is still reproducible at the repository head

values.label: History
values.meaning: Records that have reached a terminal state, plus the recorded account of how they got there where one exists.
values.cannot_justify: that a terminal state was re-checked at the repository head

values.label: Method
values.meaning: The apparatus by which a reader judges how far the rest of the record can be trusted.
values.cannot_justify: any claim about the project itself

values.label: Not requested
values.meaning: The section was not requested by the call.
values.cannot_justify: that the section is empty

values.label: Over budget
values.meaning: The item was eligible and ranked below the byte or item budget.
values.cannot_justify: that the omitted items matter less than the selected ones

attention_label.note: ADR-0010's operational definitions, reused verbatim where they apply; awaiting-verification and undiscriminated are added by get_attention.

values.label: Open
values.meaning: A finding with no terminal resolution event, ordered by severity.
values.cannot_justify: that the defect is still reproducible at the repository head

values.label: Regression
values.meaning: A currently open finding with a prior verified-fixed event.
values.cannot_justify: that the recorded repair was reverted rather than defeated another way

values.label: Unverified suspicion
values.meaning: An open candidate-concern field note.
values.cannot_justify: that the suspicion is a defect

values.label: Unknown
values.meaning: An open question.
values.cannot_justify: any answer to it

values.label: Stale knowledge
values.meaning: A claim validity interval closed at or before the reviewed head, or an obligation-bearing ledger row marked stale.
values.cannot_justify: that the recorded reading was wrong, only that it is no longer current

values.label: Awaiting verification
values.meaning: A finding whose current resolution state is fixed-pending-verification.
values.cannot_justify: that the defect is gone at the repository head

values.label: Undiscriminated
values.meaning: Two or more credible accounts stand and the record does not say which of them the evidence picks out.
values.cannot_justify: any one of the competing accounts
